page.title: Eunomia Labs, Inc.
page.description: Eunomia Labs, Inc. builds the runtime for recursive self-improvement. It profiles what AI systems do, gives them safe places to change themselves, and keeps every change inside limits the system sets.
page.bodyHtml:
Eunomia Labs, Inc. builds the runtime for recursive self-improvement (RSI). AI agents now modify their own code, tools, and infrastructure, evaluate the result, and carry what works into the next round. That loop runs on real systems: CPUs, GPUs, files, networks, and the agents themselves. Our runtime gives it three things from the system side: an accurate profile of what ran, safe points where a change can land, and limits that every change respects.

The company operates eunomia.dev, develops the projects in the eunomia-bpf GitHub organization, and is based in San Francisco, California.

One runtime, three layers

eBPF connects the three layers. The same model of small, verified programs loaded at run time observes, extends, and enforces across the kernel, userspace, and GPUs.

Profile: see what actually ran

  • AgentSight records what AI agents do on a machine. It links prompts, model calls, and tool decisions to the processes, files, and network traffic they cause, with zero instrumentation of the agent.
  • bpftime GPU support runs eBPF programs inside CUDA and ROCm kernels, so profiling reaches the code running on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs.

Change: safe places for improvements to land

  • bpftime is a userspace eBPF runtime. Applications gain uprobe and syscall extension points that load eBPF programs at run time, using the same toolchains as kernel eBPF.
  • gpu_ext turns GPU scheduling and memory management into programmable eBPF policies.
  • SchedCP lets AI agents profile a workload, then synthesize and deploy Linux scheduler policies through sched-ext.

Bound: limits every change respects

  • ActPlane enforces the policies developers already write, such as rules in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, at the operating-system level across process trees, files, and network effects, and reports each violation back to the agent.
  • AgentCgroup connects an agent's task structure to Linux resource control.

Research

Each layer comes from published systems research. bpftime appeared at OSDI 2025 as "Extending Applications Safely and Efficiently", AgentSight at PACMI 2025, and SchedCP at MLforSystem 2025. The papers page lists the full set with PDFs, artifacts, and explainers.

Open source

All code is developed in the open at github.com/eunomia-bpf, and each repository states its license. We also maintain the eunomia-bpf and wasm-bpf toolchains, the eBPF tutorials, and tutorials on CUDA, CUPTI, and NVBit. Issues and GitHub Discussions are the main collaboration channels, and the activity reports record the organization's public activity every month.

Working with us

Eunomia Labs supports teams that adopt these projects in production, from evaluation to integration. Products describes the product lines and enterprise support. To reach us directly, email yusheng@eunomia.dev.
